reader.requirement: At 1985 data-name-2 and data-name-3 must name elementary items or groups in the same logical record as the 66 entry and must not be the same item; an operand that is a 66, 77, 88 or 01 entry, or an item of another record (another WS record or another record of the same FD), must be refused.

edition-consulted.switches: below 2002 the operand candidates are the whole scope's (so a 66 alias of the record is reachable), then ResolveRedefinesPass drops one outside the record via IsWithinRegion; from 2002 the record subtree
Edition.Cite: 1985 SR4 vs 2023 SR5 citation in the COBOL2740 text; the level test (1, 66, 77) is one code at every edition

reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: the operand candidate set (whole scope at 1985, record subtree at 2002+), which changes whether an unqualified name also declared in another record is ambiguous; the refusals themselves are the same code
reader.witnesses-cover: part: legal operands, an undefined operand and the same word naming two items; not exercised are 66/77/88/01 operands, an operand of another WS record or another record of the same FD, and A THRU A

reader.notes: Every lettered prohibition is refused at --std 85 with a diagnostic; 77 and 88 operands are refused as not items of the record (COBOL1655), which is the same verdict SR4 gives (77 and 88 are not elementary items or groups of the record). A THRU A is refused through the SR8 window screen, the same-item reading the conformance determination D-85-RENAMES-SAME-NAME records.

refuter.evidence: Every refusal holds at --std 85: data-name-3 a 66 entry (E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/reread-1985-moved/out/refute-1985-m02/src/rn_d3is66.cob: COBOL2740 'data-name-3 R1 refers to an entry described with level-number 66'), an index-name operand (E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/reread-1985-moved/out/refute-1985-m02/src/rn_idx.cob: COBOL1655), a 77 (E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/reread-1985-moved/out/refute-1985-m02/src/rn_nonrec.cob: COBOL2740), plus the reader's 66/77/88/01/other-record probes. But 'RENAMES X OF G1 THRU X OF G2' (two items written with the same word X) compiles and runs (E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/reread-1985-moved/out/refute-1985-m02/src/rn_sameword.cob, runs/rn_sameword-001: R1=AABBCC). SR4 says data-name-2 and data-name-3 'cannot be the same data-name' (cite.py: 'OK  §1985:VI.5.11.3 SR4 ... the text is in SR4'), and §1985:III.2 defines a data-name as 'A user-defined word that names a data item' and says that in the general formats 'data-name' represents a word (cite.py: 'OK  §1985:III.2 (2. DEFINITIONS) the text is in the clause'). Under that reading SR4 forbids the same WORD, qualified or not, and the program must be refused. The same-ITEM reading also leaves SR4's clause redundant: SR8 already refuses one item as both operands (cite.py: 'OK  §1985:VI.5.11.3 SR8'). The compiler follows the other reading, recorded as docs/conformance/3/D-85-RENAMES-SAME-NAME.md (same item, chosen by GnuCOBOL precedence because it treats the text as leaving a choice). The verdict rests on that reading, which the 1985 definition of data-name puts in doubt; the reader's notes call the A THRU A refusal the SR4 refusal without testing the two-item, one-word form.
refuter.corrected: CONFORMS only under the same-item reading of D-85-RENAMES-SAME-NAME; under the §1985:III.2 reading (a data-name is a word) 'RENAMES X OF G1 THRU X OF G2' must be refused and is accepted (under-rejects). The determination should be re-ruled on the 1985 definition before the row is closed.
